name: worldquest

scripts.generate: pnpm design:tokens && pnpm i18n:types && pnpm edge:build
scripts.verify: pnpm generate && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm content:validate && pnpm content:crosscheck && pnpm content:preview --quiet && pnpm i18n:check && pnpm design:contrast && pnpm lint:a11y && pnpm escape-hatches && pnpm reachability && pnpm check:sql && pnpm five-states && pnpm scrollable && pnpm engines:simulate && pnpm check:eas
scripts.$comment:typecheck:edge: The edge modules were the only TypeScript here nobody typechecked: Vitest transforms them with esbuild, which strips types without checking them, so `pnpm test` went green on code `tsc` rejects — and it is the code that verifies signatures and decides who has paid. Four real defects on the first run. The Deno entrypoints stay excluded; see supabase/tsconfig.json.
scripts.$comment:e2e: Exports the real bundle through Metro and drives it in Chromium via react-native-web. Not a device — see apps/mobile/e2e/flow.cjs for exactly what that does and does not prove. The export step is the point as much as the driving: it is the only thing in this repo that runs the bundler.
scripts.e2e: pnpm --filter @worldquest/mobile exec expo export --platform web --output-dir ../../node_modules/.cache/wq-web && node apps/mobile/e2e/flow.cjs node_modules/.cache/wq-web node_modules/.cache/wq-e2e-shots
scripts.$comment:design:shots: Screenshots any set of routes from the exported bundle at 320/390/768 and reports the things a picture cannot show — touch targets under 44pt, sideways scroll, unlabelled controls. Feeds /design-review. Never a gate: verify and e2e are the gates.
scripts.design:shots: pnpm --filter @worldquest/mobile exec expo export --platform web --output-dir ../../node_modules/.cache/wq-web && node scripts/design-shots.cjs
scripts.$comment:bundle:native: Bundles for iOS and Android, and enforces a per-platform size budget. Until this existed the app had only ever been bundled for web, and Metro resolves per platform — a native-only resolution failure was invisible. The budget is here because Hermes reads the whole bundle before the first frame, making size the one cold-start input measurable without a phone. Proves the graph compiles and is not growing quietly; NOT that the app runs.
scripts.$comment:build:flags: Rasterises the 65 country flags from flag-icons (MIT) into apps/mobile/assets/flags. Flags sat in the 'needs an illustrator' bucket for the whole project, which was wrong: a national flag is a public-domain drawing somebody has already got right, and drawing one from memory is the wrong-fact bug asset-prompts.md forbids. Run it when the country list changes; the PNGs are committed, so it is not part of verify.
scripts.$comment:build:maps: Projects and rasterises the region + country outlines from Natural Earth (via world-atlas, public domain) into apps/mobile/assets/geo. Map thumbnails were filed as 'needs an illustrator' for the whole project — the third time that mistake was made, after sound and flags — while asset-prompts.md listed geometry under NEVER GENERATE and named Natural Earth in the same row. Run it when the country list changes; the PNGs are committed, so it is not part of verify.
scripts.$comment:build:icons: Rasterises the UI icon set from Lucide (ISC) into apps/mobile/assets/icons as white-on-transparent alpha masks, recoloured at runtime with tintColor. The fourth false blocker after sound, flags and geometry: asset-prompts.md has named Lucide and Phosphor since it was written, while the tab bar shipped '⌂ ◎ ◈ ☺ ⋯' as literal text — a different typeface on every device, four of them colour emoji, none of them mirroring for RTL. Run it when the icon set changes; the PNGs are committed, so it is not part of verify.
scripts.$comment:build:art: Derives every shipped illustration and the four app icons from the delivered masters in docs/design/assets — resize, letterbox onto the canvas colour, compress to the per-asset budget, and write apps/mobile/src/lib/art.generated.ts. The masters are 1536x1024 PNGs with alpha; the store rules are not: an iOS icon must be square and opaque, and an Android adaptive icon must be inset to survive an arbitrary mask. Deriving rather than hand-exporting is what keeps those four in step with the art they came from. Run it when the masters change; the output is committed, so it is not part of verify.
scripts.$comment:import:art: Files a raw art delivery into docs/design/assets under the names the code actually imports — region codes for continents, the title ladder for levels, the category segment for glyphs. Refuses anything it cannot map rather than filing it plausibly: a master under a name no screen imports ships as unreachable bytes, which has happened twice and is invisible when it does.
scripts.$comment:build:store: The store listing art that can be derived from what the repo already owns — the two store icons, the Play feature graphic, and the wordmark set in the app's own typeface. NOT the screenshots: asset-prompts.md §14 marks their required pixel sizes TODO(verify) because Apple changes them, and a guessed canvas size is a rejected submission.
scripts.$comment:build:store:shots: The six store screenshots from asset-prompts.md §14, composed from the REAL app at the two sizes Apple requires — read off Apple's own spec rather than remembered, because a guessed canvas size is a rejected submission. Drives the app the way the E2E does, since two of the six shots need a lesson played. Play is absent: its requirements live on hosts this session's egress policy blocks.
scripts.$comment:build:locations: Derives facts.locations.v1.json from the `subregion` already declared on every entity, so a country's location fact can never disagree with its own entity. Invents no geography — it is a projection of data the pack holds. Run it when the country list changes; the JSON is committed, so it is not part of verify.
scripts.$comment:db:types: A script, not one line, because the committed file carries a 'do not hand-edit' header and single-quoted literals that the generator emits double-quoted — both applied by hand, once. CI ran the raw command and diffed the result, so that check compared a decorated file against an undecorated one and could never pass, however fresh the types were. The decoration now lives in the generator: one command, run by humans and by CI, whose output is exactly what is committed. --local, not --project-id: migrations are the source of truth, and the hosted project is currently a migration behind.
scripts.$comment:db:harness: Applies every migration to a REAL Postgres and then exercises the reward paths — the quest, the achievement tiers, all four purchases, and what a signed-in client may not do. Written because `supabase db reset` and `supabase test db` need Docker, which no environment this repo has been built in has had: five hundred lines of PL/pgSQL that decides what a user is paid had never been EXECUTED, only read. It needs the postgresql-16 server binaries and a non-root user, so it is not in `verify`; `supabase test db` and its pgTAP suite are still the real check, and this catches the class of thing that stops that suite ever running. Proven to fail: removing the `on conflict do nothing` behind the achievement award turns it red.
scripts.$comment:edge:build: Verifies the deploy bundle is self-contained AND writes its generated half — `_content/answers.ts`, the fact→entity answer key derived from the packs. Until this wrote anything, the function on disk imported a file no checkout had ever contained, so `supabase start` and `supabase functions deploy` both failed on it. Part of `generate`, so a fresh clone can start the local stack.
scripts.$comment:edge:deploy: store-notifications deploys with --no-verify-jwt because Apple is not a user and holds no JWT. That is not a weaker check: the store's own signature — a pinned chain, a per-payload ECDSA signature, and an audience check that the notification is about our bundle — is a stronger claim than a JWT is.
scripts.edge:deploy: supabase functions deploy submit-lesson --project-ref tjdjogidudjobxipibqb && supabase functions deploy store-notifications --no-verify-jwt --project-ref tjdjogidudjobxipibqb
scripts.$comment:screenshot: `.png=dataurl` rather than `file`: this harness emits ONE standalone HTML file into a cache directory and shoots it there, so a relative asset path would resolve to nothing and every flag would render blank — which looks exactly like the placeholder it replaced. Inlining costs ~900 KB in a throwaway file and cannot half-work. The four `@worldquest/*` aliases are because pnpm links workspace packages into each package's OWN node_modules, not the root's — and this command runs from the root, so esbuild could resolve none of them. It had been failing to build for long enough that the paywall, which only this harness can render with prices, had never been re-shot.
scripts.screenshot: esbuild scripts/screenshot/render.tsx --bundle --platform=node --format=cjs --jsx=automatic --alias:react-native=react-native-web --alias:@worldquest/design=./packages/design/src/index.ts --alias:@worldquest/engines=./packages/engines/src/index.ts --alias:@worldquest/i18n=./packages/i18n/src/index.ts --alias:@worldquest/analytics=./packages/analytics/src/index.ts --define:__DEV__=false --alias:expo-linear-gradient=./scripts/screenshot/linear-gradient-web.tsx --loader:.json=json --loader:.png=dataurl --loader:.webp=dataurl --outfile=node_modules/.cache/wq-render.cjs && node node_modules/.cache/wq-render.cjs > node_modules/.cache/wq-app.html && node scripts/screenshot/shoot.cjs node_modules/.cache/wq-app.html docs/design/assets/screens
scripts.$comment:escape-hatches: Fails on `any`, @ts-expect-error, @ts-ignore or eslint-disable outside tests. PROJECT.md §12 has banned all four since week one and nothing checked — the DoD ✅ rested on nobody having broken it yet. Deliberate exceptions live in an allowlist with a written reason, and a stale entry fails the same as a violation.
scripts.$comment:check:eas: The two config files an iOS build reads before it compiles anything. Both of the first two TestFlight runs died on one of them, on a 10x-billed macOS runner, having compiled nothing: eas.json rejects unknown keys (including the $comment convention used in this very line), and app.json identified no EAS project so eas build refused to guess an owning account. Strict JSON, schema keys only, no committed App Store Connect credentials, and an owner or a projectId. Detail in docs/engineering/eas-build-profiles.md.
scripts.$comment:check:ios-creds: Asks EAS whether the project holds an Apple distribution certificate and an App Store provisioning profile. NOT in verify: it needs the network and an EXPO_TOKEN. It is the one iOS build prerequisite this repo cannot satisfy — `eas build --non-interactive` refuses to mint credentials, so without them every TestFlight run fails on a 10x-billed macOS runner. Both workflows run it on their cheap job; run it yourself with EXPO_TOKEN set.
scripts.$comment:a11y:tree: Walks Chromium's computed accessibility tree over ten routes — the thing a screen reader actually consumes. lint:a11y reads source and design:shots accepts textContent as a label, so a button whose only content is an emoji passed both. This is the mechanical half of the VoiceOver/TalkBack box; the manual pass in docs/plan/device-pass.md is still required.
scripts.a11y:tree: pnpm --filter @worldquest/mobile exec expo export --platform web --output-dir ../../node_modules/.cache/wq-web && node scripts/a11y-tree.cjs
scripts.$comment:verify: CLAUDE.md calls this "all of it, and the gate that matters", and it was neither. `engines:simulate` gates the economy on twelve health checks and ran only in CI, so a reward change could be pushed without ever meeting it. `content:preview --quiet` catches a question that reads as nonsense while validating fine — three of those have shipped. Both are seconds and both are now here. `verify:full` carries the three that need a browser or a bundler; CI runs that one.
scripts.$comment:verify:full: `verify` plus everything needing Chromium or Metro. `bundle:native` and `a11y:tree` were written for two specific bugs that were invisible without them — a native-only module resolution failure, and a control with no accessible name that lint:a11y and design:shots both passed — and then neither was wired into CI or into verify. A check nothing runs is a check that does not exist, which is the exact failure both were built to end.
scripts.verify:full: pnpm verify && pnpm bundle:native && pnpm e2e && pnpm a11y:tree

$comment: Install from the repo ROOT, never inside a package. See CLAUDE.md.
